subject: Civil Engineering
title: Forces on a Dam
description: Learn Forces on a Dam in one minute.

hook.text: A dam fights multiple enemies at once — water, silt, ice, earthquakes, and its own weight.

buildup.text: Hydrostatic pressure increases linearly with depth — the base bears the greatest force.

discovery.text: Silt accumulates behind the dam — adding horizontal pressure beyond water alone.

twist.text: Earthquake forces act horizontally — shaking both the dam and the water behind it.

climax.text: The dam must resist overturning, sliding, and overstressing — checked for every load combination.

punchline.text: A dam stands against water, earth, ice, and earthquakes. It must win every battle.

quiz.question: Why does the base of a dam experience the greatest hydrostatic pressure?
options: Water flows fastest at the base, creating more pressure
Hydrostatic pressure increases linearly with depth — the deepest point has the most
The dam's own weight concentrates at the base
